items.title: In tilt app e siti delle principali banche Usa. Guasto ai sistemi di United Airlines, poi risolto
items.summary: Dopo il caso di Microsoft e gli aerei a terra. Chase Bank: 'Nessuna prova di cyberattacco, è un bug nel software' La Federal Reserve funziona regolarmente. La compagnia aerea cala a Wall Street: 'E' un problema tecnico'
items.content:
A pochi giorni dal collasso globale di Microsoft e dal blocco a terra di tutti i voli, le infrastrutture digitali negli Stati Uniti si fermano di nuovo. Le principali banche americane - tra cui JpMorgan-Chase Bank of America, Wells Fargo e U.S. Bank - hanno riscontrato diffusi disservizi nei servizi di banking online e nelle procedure di accesso. Una sequenza di eventi che, sebbene al momento privi di collegamento, dimostra la fragilità di un intero sistema.

E n uovi disagi anche per il trasporto aereo americano . United Airlines segnala un'interruzione generalizzata dei suoi sistemi. "Ci scusiamo per l'inconveniente. Siamo a conoscenza dell'interruzione del sistema su vasta scala e i nostri team si stanno impegnando al massimo per ripristinare il corretto funzionamento nel minor tempo possibile", mette in evidenza United Airlines su X.

No n ci sono indicazioni che l'interruzione dei sistemi sia un cyberattacco. Lo ha detto un portavoce di United Airlines citando alcune fonti. "Stiamo risolvendo un problema tecnico che riguarda i voli in partenza. Non c'è alcun impatto sui voli in corso", ha messo in evidenza United Airlines.

Poco dopo United Airlines ha affermato di aver risolto il problema tecnico che ha causato ritardi ai suoi voli.

Anche Chase Bank afferma che i disservizi ai suoi sistemi sarebbero dovuti a un "problema temporaneo causato da un bug nel suo software" che potrebbe provocare disagi ad altre banche. La banca precisa che non si tratta di un "problema sistemico" né di un cyberattacco . "JPMorgan Chase ha riscontrato un problema temporaneo legato a un bug del software nei sistemi hardware locali. Non ci sono prove che si tratti di un attacco informatico. L'assistenza ad alcuni clienti sta richiedendo più tempo del solito", afferma Chase Bank. "Qualora le transazioni con altre banche fossero coinvolte, questi istituti potrebbero essere stati interessati ma non si tratta di un problema sistemico", ha messo in evidenza.

Sono stati gli utenti in mattinata a segnalare alle banche le difficoltà che stavano riscontrando: migliaia di persone che hanno lamentato difficoltà nell'accesso tramite web e app mobile , nonché problemi con i trasferimenti di denaro. La banca più colpita è stata JpMorgan Chase con oltre 4.600 4.600 segnalazioni, seguita da Bank of America con oltre 2.000.

L'assistenza di Chase è stata la più tempestiva ad intervenire prima con un messaggio agli utenti e poi con l'assistenza che ha confermato il disservizio, dichiarando di essere al lavoro per risolvere un problema tecnico che sta interessando le piattaforme di banking online.

"A causa di un problema tecnico, il completamento di alcune transazioni sta richiedendo più tempo del solito, ma i clienti continuano ad avere accesso ai propri conti e ai propri fondi», ha dichiarato l'istituto in un comunicato. "Stiamo lavorando per risolvere la situazione il più rapidamente possibile". Mentre una fonte informata ha spiegato a Fox Business che si tratta di "un bug tecnico, non un problema informatico".

Per ora insomma non ci sarebbe alcuna conferma che possa esserci un attacco informatico dietro i disservizi, e le verifiche condotte dalle stesse banche e dalle autorità finanziarie continuano ad indicare che il problema può essere stato causato da guasti tecnici interni, escludendo un'azione coordinata da parte di hacker.

Intanto la banca centrale americana, la Federal Reserve, ha assicurato che i suoi sistemi interbancari (Fedwire, FedACH e FedNow) funzionano regolarmente senza anomalie. Questo potrebbe confermare che il blocco riguarda i portali di accesso per i clienti (siti web e app) e non le reti fondamentali del sistema finanziario. Le banche hanno, inoltre, rassicurato i correntisti sul fatto che i fondi e i dati sensibili non sono stati compromessi, precisando che i team tecnici stanno lavorando per ripristinare la piena operatività.

Il problema alle app e a servizi di alcune delle maggiori banche americane sarebbe tecnico e sarebbe stato iniziato da un'interruzione in casa Chase che avrebbe poi avuto ripercussioni sulle altre banche. Lo riporta Cnn citando alcune fonti.

items.title: Show HN: Sutra-OS – A self-hosted ontology platform
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/0nelight/sutra-os Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50525052 Points: 21 # Comments: 3
items.content:
An open-source, self-hosted ontology platform. Your data becomes one model you own: typed, linked, changed only through rules the server enforces, and every number traces back to its source.

Quick start · How it works · Proposals · Python SDK · Contributing

Beta. Only small parts are still alpha: the model language and APIs may still change between versions, and parts of the user interface and docs are unfinished.

Maintainers wanted. Sutra-OS is a one-person project so far. See Contributing .

Sutra-OS began in late 2025 as a thought experiment: a free version of the system described in Ontology-Oriented Software Development , whose creators I deeply admire.

Much talent today goes into software that sells attention, while the software everything else runs on is mostly free: by a rough estimate, 70–90% of US economic output depends on free software at some critical point. That openness is not guaranteed. In November 2026, Nvidia's board parted with the founder who had its AI models released openly. Sutra-OS adds to the commons under the AGPL, so that it stays readable by anyone.

The past ten years have shown what it costs when nobody can see what depends on what. In 2017, NotPetya spread through a single Ukrainian accounting program and stopped Maersk's ports and Merck's factories. In 2023, a corrupted file in one FAA system halted every domestic departure in the US. In 2024, one faulty CrowdStrike update crashed millions of Windows machines, and airlines, hospitals and banks stood still. In November 2026, a single vendor took Outlook down for a day and some cities went back to fax. That same week, data flooded the FAA's telecommunications network, aging routers buckled, and the US saw only the third nationwide ground stop in its history. No one, it seems, had those routers on the map of what keeps planes in the air, so no one could ask beforehand what would stop if they failed.

That question is what Sutra-OS is built for. Every system, device, dataset and decision becomes an object with links to what it feeds and what feeds it, and every number can be traced back to its source. Whoever holds such a model can ask, before the outage, what stops when one piece fails, and get an answer, at every scale from a single person to a government (hopefully never a world government). Many small ontologies, each held by those it describes, keep power spread out; one model of everything would not.

Almost everyone. Whoever you are, someone else keeps a better-connected record of your affairs than you do. Sutra is for anyone who wants their own.

Requirements: Linux x86_64, JDK 21, the Clojure CLI , Node.js, Python 3, git.

This starts an embedded PostgreSQL and the server on 127.0.0.1 and prints the address. Data lives in $SUTRA_HOME (default ~/.local/share/sutra ). The admin password is in zugang.edn ("access") there. Run the bin/sutra bind … line it prints once.

Three ideas carry the whole platform: object types , link types and action types . The examples below use the farm model in resources/presets .

You start by saying what exists: a lot of hay, from one field and one cut; a sale, to one buyer. Each is a typed thing with a kind and a key.

Nobody types or counts :in-barn : it is the bales made minus every bale sold, computed by the server. :bales is an integer, so "about forty" or -3 is refused before anything is written.

An object type is a typed table with a name, a face in the UI and a class in the generated SDK. Properties are typed, constrained and can be derived , so a value nobody typed in still shows up like any other column.

A sale on its own is just a number. A sale linked to the lot it came out of is a fact everyone can see.

The sale names its lot and the link follows it: from the lot you see its sales, from a sale its lot, and :connected-sum above sums across that link. One line, and the barn knows what is in it.

Links are first-class: named in both directions, navigable in the UI, traversable in the SDK ( lot.sales ), and usable in derived values, filters and object sets.

In most systems anybody may change anything, and nobody can say who did. Here there is no "update row". There are only actions : named decisions with typed inputs and rules the server enforces. Selling hay is one of them, and it has a condition.

Ask to sell more bales than are in the barn and the server refuses and says why, with the same sentence for the phone, the CLI, the Python script and the AI agent. A refused action writes nothing. Every sale records who made it, and nobody can put someone else's name there.

Actions are the only write path: typed parameters, validation, submission criteria and state transitions, defined once and enforced everywhere.

Every rule you would otherwise keep in your head has this shape: a fact the server computes, and an action that checks it. Declare it once, and stop remembering it.

The same three ideas run the arable side of the farm. A field's margin is derived from its paid harvests and the hay sold off it, two links away. A harvest moves from planted to harvested , delivered and paid only through its actions, and Sell harvest refuses to run without a signed delivery note and a quality test of your own.

In most software, deciding and doing are one step. In Sutra they are two. When you sell hay, the server first writes down what would change: one new sale, forty bales, your name on it. Nothing has happened yet. Only when that note is approved does the barn change.

And it is not a promise. A test fails if the part that decides ever does anything but decide.

Your data comes in as it is. Mail over IMAP, CSV exports, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and SSH, shaped by transforms in Python, SQL or Clojure.

Every number has a past. Lineage runs from each object back through the transforms and datasets to the mail, statement or row it came from ( sutra lineage ). When someone else's figures disagree with yours, you open the source.

Agents get only the tools you name. An action, a function, a query on one type. By default ( :writes :propose ) their changes are staged as proposals; a rejected one doesn't come back, and the model's prompt and answer are kept with the run.

The model is versioned like code. Model and data live on branches. You stage a change, commit it, open a proposal, see who consumes what you touched, and merge into main only when it's reviewed. Webhooks and notifications stay silent on a branch unless you say otherwise.

Share exactly what you choose. Markings on types and properties are mandatory access control; grants on projects decide who may read, act and invoke. A group (a co-op, a tenants' association, a family) can pool what its members agree to share, and nothing else, and the server enforces it on every read: lists, filters, counts and totals. One person's data can't show what everyone else was offered. A group's can.

Builders and users are different people. One person writes the model; everyone else gets apps with the build tools locked away, and a server that says no when no is the right answer.

Secrets stay out of reach. A separate egress agent holds every external credential, so the code that reads your mail never sees the password.

You described the farm once. Generate a Python SDK from it, and your code speaks the farm's language: lots , harvests and buyers , and the things you are allowed to do with them, not tables and joins.

farm_sdk.py is plain, typed Python: a class per object type, an attribute per property and link, a method per action with the action's parameters as its signature. Sutra's language server ( clients/ent-lsp ) runs pyright for Python and labels each completion as what it is in the model ( property , link-type , action , state ); any editor that lets you pick the language server can run it ( Neovim config ).

An action is a method. Its signature comes from the model; a missing argument is flagged before anything runs.

States are types. A harvest's status is Literal['planted', 'harvested', 'delivered', 'paid'] , so the editor offers exactly those four.

Filters are checked too. Comparing bales with a string, or reading a link that may be empty, fails in the editor, not on the farm.

An object, not a row. A lot brings its derived values and its links along. Nobody stored in_barn ; the server computes it.

Act on it. Selling hay is something you do to a lot . The server checks the rule, writes the sale, stamps your name on it and tells you what changed.

Ask first, or only propose. The same call can be a question (nothing is written) or a proposal (staged until someone approves it). That is how an agent gets to use it.

Walk a lifecycle. A harvest goes from planted to harvested , delivered and paid , one action per step, and the rules travel with them. The states are declared in the model, so status is typed Literal['planted', 'harvested', 'delivered', 'paid'] and your editor offers exactly those four.

Ask the whole farm, in one line. Who bought how much hay, month by month, at what price. Grouped, summed and sorted on the server; nothing is downloaded to be counted.

items.title: '007 Usa, Iran sta sviluppando piani per bomba sporca a Washington'
items.summary: La Cnn: 'Al momento pianificazione, nessun segnale di un attacco imminente'. La Casa Bianca: 'Non ci sono minacce credibili da Teheran'
items.content:
L'Iran sta elaborando piani per colpire esponenti dell'amministrazione Trump ricorrendo alla detonazione di una 'bomba sporca' o all'impiego di un'arma chimica a Washington. Lo riporta Cnn citando sette funzionari dell'intelligence americana, secondo le quali al momento l'Iran sta cercando di dotarsi di varie opzioni e non c'è per ora l'indicazione di un attacco imminente. I piani intercettati dagli Stati Uniti sono molto dettagliati e includono luoghi e obiettivi specifici.

"Monitoriamo tutte le potenziali minacce, ma al momento non ci sono minacce credibili". Lo ha detto la portavoce della Casa Bianca Lauren Bis a Cnn commentando le indiscrezioni sui piani dell'Iran per l'uso di una bomba sporca per colpire funzionari dell'amministrazione Trump a Washington.

items.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
items.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
items.content:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024 .

Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.

"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.

The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.

Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.

The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.

Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries .

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."

The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place.

According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news di oggi. Raid russi sui ponti di Kiev. Nuovo attacco al ponte di Crimea, traffico sospeso
items.summary: Il sindaco della capitale ucraina Klitschko: colpiti i ponti Nord e Sud. Forti esplosioni nella città. Mosca denuncia il secondo attacco ucraino in 24 ore al ponte che collega la Russia alla penisola annessa
items.content:
Attacchi ai ponti su entrambi i fronti della guerra in Ucraina. Due importanti infrastrutture di Kiev sono state colpite da raid russi, secondo quanto riferito dal sindaco Vitali Klitschko . Nella capitale sono state udite diverse forti esplosioni. Intanto Mosca denuncia un nuovo attacco ucraino al ponte di Crimea , il secondo in 24 ore. Il traffico sull'infrastruttura che collega la Russia alla penisola annessa è stato sospeso.

Mosca: nuovo attacco ucraino al ponte di Crimea, traffico sospeso

Le forze armate ucraine hanno attaccato nuovamente il ponte di Crimea , per la seconda volta in 24 ore . Lo ha denunciato il governatore russo della penisola annessa da Mosca, Serghei Aksyonov. “Il nemico ha attaccato ancora una volta il ponte di Crimea. Al momento, il traffico è stato sospeso. Forniremo ulteriori aggiornamenti con l'evolversi della situazione”, ha scritto su Telegram, secondo quanto riportato dalla Tass .

Due importanti ponti di Kiev sono stati colpiti da attacchi russi. Lo ha riferito il sindaco Vitali Klitschko , precisando che, secondo le prime informazioni, i raid hanno interessato i ponti Nord e Sud della capitale. Poco prima, l'aeronautica militare ucraina aveva lanciato un allarme per l'arrivo di missili. Alcuni giornalisti dell' Afp hanno udito diverse forti esplosioni in città, mentre sui social circolano immagini, non ancora verificate, che sembrerebbero mostrare un'esplosione su almeno uno dei ponti che attraversano il fiume Dnipro .

items.title: Optimizely Compromised, Served Malware on Zoom, GitLab
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.report-uri.com/worlds-largest-brands-infected-with-malware-via-optimizely/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50524767 Points: 61 # Comments: 19
items.content:
On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock .

This is exactly the kind of attack Report URI is designed to detect. Our platform can identify unexpected changes to trusted JavaScript, detect new scripts being loaded and reveal suspicious connections to external destinations. In this case, those signals would have exposed the malicious activity, even though the original script was being served from a trusted Optimizely domain. With an appropriate CSP in enforcement mode, organisations could have gone a step further and blocked key parts of the attack before they succeeded.

The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy . A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed. At 21:52 UTC we found it in only 1 of the 188 infected snippets, down from 169 at 20:56 UTC. If your site uses Optimizely Web, or you visited any of the sites below today, read on.

Optimizely Web works by having each customer load a JavaScript "snippet" from Optimizely's CDN, for example https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js . The snippet contains Optimizely's code, the customer's experiments and an optional field called Project JavaScript ( projectJS ): custom code the customer writes in their Optimizely dashboard, which runs on every page.

The attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects, and the rest of each snippet was untouched. The file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com , with Optimizely's certificate, from a host that every affected site already trusted. Here is what was added to Zoom's snippet:

Some customers serve their snippet from their own domain, such as opt.scheels.com/js/ .js or www.vodafone.com.au/js/ .js . Those were affected too, because the content comes from the same Optimizely project.

We don't know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else. That's for Optimizely to explain. To be clear, Optimizely's CDN served exactly what it was given; this was not a CDN cache-poisoning attack. Optimizely's own sites were affected as well: the snippets for www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com both carried the code.

The payload was rebuilt 26 times during the day. The attacker added features, and added wallets but never removed any.

Every visitor received the same script, track.js , and every part of it was active at once. What a visitor experienced depended on their device and what they did on the page.

The script finds any valid wallet address (BTC, ETH and EVM chains, TRON, Solana, TON, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin) and replaces it with one of the attacker's. It validates checksums so it only swaps real addresses. It swaps them in:

It re-scans the page whenever it changes. Copy an address from any affected page, or from anywhere else while that tab is open, and you may paste the attacker's.

Added at 13:43 UTC. The script watches form submissions and every fetch /XHR POST for a card number (Luhn-checked), expiry date and CVV. When it has all three, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php with navigator.sendBeacon . Cards entered in hosted payment iframes (Stripe, Adyen and similar) were out of its reach. Cards typed into a site's own form fields were not.

When it swaps an address next to wallet or payment wording, it sends the following to https://1688360.cc/hit.php :

On iPhones and iPads the script loads boot.js from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu . It reads the iOS version and loads an exploit chain in a hidden iframe:

The Coruna loader is byte-identical to a sample we analysed in October from a different campaign. The kit's own comments say iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, are patched. Pages on iOS 18.6 or earlier reload every 60 seconds to retry the exploit, which is a visible symptom.

As of 19:25 UTC on 16 November, the attacker's wallets had received about $7,040 , all within roughly nine hours on the 16th:

We fetched 1,611 distinct Optimizely snippets , found mostly through our own crawl data, and checked each one for the malicious code. 188 snippets belonging to 178 organisations were infected. We kept a copy of every infected file, along with its response headers, SHA-256 hash and fetch time as evidence. The real number is likely higher as we could only check snippets we could find in time.

Ranked by Tranco position within each sector and the status at 21:52 UTC: every snippet except TalkTalk's had been cleaned.

The earlier webshell.lol wave, through Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute Media, affected other sites and isn't included above.

Every one of these needs only a CSP in Report-Only mode, so nothing on the site breaks:

It's possible to go even further and deploy a CSP that could actively block these attacks and prevent any data breach happening. The websites affected by this attack weren't necessarily running vulnerable code of their own, they were loading JavaScript from a provider they trusted, and that trust was exploited. This is why monitoring what runs in your visitors' browsers is so important. Report URI gives organisations the visibility to detect when trusted dependencies change or behave unexpectedly, and the tools to help enforce policies that prevent malicious scripts and connections from succeeding.

We crawled 256 of the affected organisations' own hosts and evaluated their CSP against what this payload needs:

Allowing cdn.optimizely.com was never going to help. The malicious code arrived from the trusted host itself. What separated the 24 protected sites from the rest was a restrictive script-src . A site that lists only the hosts it needs blocks 1688360.cc . Two common settings let it straight through:

All of these domains are attacker-owned; block them including subdomains.

Attacker wallets: BTC 19g9rZcPeiz8rUvyWpTRyXXhPnjsWrc3kW ETH/EVM 0xC4026b06D82b0F0B363eda0642D61CfbDc17884e TRON THvs6p56XkUiMkJeSc51cAP64u2RsTYqxa SOL FVtL8NMYS9PA1v3HE67XUGCtGA9JaZUvqav2fU2LrV5n TON UQAgM1VqSZQiJLSG5w-ovurq5CZdxLEK3_7CMmwALTA5e09p LTC ltc1q3wp7g6ds0ggg6fl6kncpa4sepn0q3qfacgred5 BCH qzkaaf8n6grmpr0d9lx8xutn3r9lk722f566hhpe58 DOGE DBEGrxRF7KMSuhTS4c1MFviStU6efdMnu5

We keep an archive of every infected snippet with hashes and timestamps, and can share it with affected organisations and CERTs on request. During research and investigation, once we were confident that Optimizely was the source, we began efforts to reach out via various channels and provide the full details. At the time of publication, we have not had any response.

items.title: Il Papa colpito da un rosario al volto, ma nessuna conseguenza
items.summary: Spesso i fedeli gli lanciano oggetti mentre sta sulla Papamobile
items.content:
Piccolo incidente senza conseguenze per il Papa durante il suo giro sulla Papamobile tra la folla della spianata di Las Palmas, prima della Messa, l'ultima in terra peruviana. Un fedele, come capita spesso, ha lanciato verso Leone XIV un rosario. Stavolta però il piccolo oggetto ha raggiunto all'occhio Papa Prevost, una scena ripresa dalle telecamere.

Il gesto del pontefice di toccarsi l'occhio ha suscitato preoccupazione tra i presenti, ma immediatamente dopo s'è capito che non era successo niente di grave. Il Papa non ha quindi interrotto il suo percorso e subito dopo ha celebrato serenamente la Santa Messa. Pochi giorni fa è successa una cosa simile: una ragazza ha lanciato il suo rosario verso il Papa, sempre a bordo della Papamobile. Quella volta, con ottimo riflesso, il Papa lo ha preso in mano, lo ha benedetto e lo ha restituito alla proprietaria.

items.title: Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use
items.summary: Article URL: https://xusheng.dev/posts/windows-coding-agent-telemetry/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50524736 Points: 152 # Comments: 62
items.content:
I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe , claude.exe , copilot.exe , and cursor.exe , alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , and code.exe .

Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools?

The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll . I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the "optional" diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft.

I shared the initial finding on X . This post includes more details about the investigation behind it.

Opening the DLL in Binary Ninja made the first lead easy to see. These were explicit executable names embedded in a Windows component:

Following the references showed that the names were used in comparisons. There are four CLI-agent slots checking copilot.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , and agy.exe , with extensionless equivalents on the WSL route. Five desktop-agent slots check github.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , cursor.exe , and antigravity.exe .

The compiler-generated C++ names are unwieldy, so I will call these functions executable-name matchers . For reference, one related matcher is std::_Func_impl_no_alloc , bool, std::basic_string_view > const&, Microsoft::Diagnostics::MissionControlAggregator::Utils::AppType>::_Do_call . The screenshot shows another lambda instantiation performing the same kind of name comparison.

The feature guarding the new agent checks has a particularly direct name: CLICodingAgentUsage , feature ID 62580080 .

And the list extends beyond AI agents. The same component checks for node.exe , python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , clang.exe , gdb.exe , javac.exe , devenv.exe , and code.exe , among others. Those checks feed broader developer-tool categories. Some of these checks also verify the publisher: the Node.js slot expects Node.js Foundation , Python expects Python Software Foundation , and the .NET and Visual Studio slots expect Microsoft Corporation . The compiler/debugger group containing GCC and Clang has no additional publisher check in this path.

The next question was whether the component scans running processes itself. Following Aggregator::OnLoad revealed that it subscribes to existing Windows events instead.

For Windows programs, it consumes KernelProcess.AppStateChangeSummary and Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary . These provide application identities that its handlers parse and pass to the matchers. For WSL, it consumes Microsoft.Windows.Lxss.Manager.Exec and ExecCritical , using the imageName field. A regular Windows codex.exe can therefore reach the CLI-agent checks through the app-state summary route; this is not limited to Linux programs running inside WSL.

A successful match sets a slot in the aggregator's state. Later, ReportCohorts turns those slots into bitsets and emits a report named Segments.SubCohorts . The numbers correspond to twelve broader tool categories, four CLI agents, and five desktop agents.

ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) is the mechanism carrying that report. In this case, it is a self-describing TraceLogging event. Rather than writing the executable names into every report, the component assigns each category a bit. A set Codex bit means the matching tool was observed during the reporting window.

The source events also include runtime, time in focus, interaction counters, and resource usage. This component appears to discard those details and record only a bitmap of which agents were observed. The report's timestamps describe the collection window, not how long each agent was used.

Although I found no prompt text or source code in this report, collecting which agents and developer tools someone uses already has significant privacy implications.

Strings and code are a useful lead, but I wanted to see the component running. I checked my Parallels Windows 11 ARM64 VM, build 26200.9974 . Its MissionControlAggregator.dll was version 10.0.26100.9818 , and CLICodingAgentUsage was already enabled as a service experiment. I had not manually enabled the feature.

DiagTrack, the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service, was also already running with its startup type set to Automatic . It starts a separate AggregatorHost.exe process, and that process loads the DLL. The following administrative PowerShell commands show the service, its child process, and the loaded module:

The process IDs connect the pieces: DiagTrack runs in process 10148 , which is the parent of AggregatorHost.exe , process 1500 ; the module listing places MissionControlAggregator.dll inside that child.

The public ISO's baseline VM had the coding-agent feature disabled by image default, so the evidence does not support saying that it is active on every Windows installation. On my ARM64 VM, however, the relevant feature and service were active before the test.

To test the finding in practice, I copied cmd.exe to a file named codex.exe and ran it in the interactive Windows session. The name alone was enough for the component to recognize it as Codex.

I captured an AppStateChangeSummary for the running process from the KernelProcess provider ( {2839ff94-8f12-4e1b-82e3-af7af77a450f} ), with LaunchCount=1 and TerminateCount=0 . The aggregator's saved state contained the value 2 in CLI slot 2, the Codex slot. A separate run without an additional ETW trace also set that slot, confirming that detection worked through Windows' existing diagnostic collection.

The report normally follows a roughly daily boundary. To capture it immediately, I temporarily moved the saved reporting-window start 25 hours into the past and restarted DiagTrack with a trace listening for the aggregator. The resulting Segments.SubCohorts event contained:

The value 4 is 1 : the Codex CLI bit. The name had made it through the input summary, the matcher, the persisted state, and the emitted report.

I also tested the developer-tool path separately, using a copy of cmd.exe named gcc.exe . It set developer-tool slot 3. With optional diagnostic data allowed, I found the resulting Segments.SubCohorts event in DiagTrack's upload queue with SubCohorts: [8] ( 1 ). This is the compiler/debugger category shared by GCC, Clang, and related tools, rather than a separate bit for each executable.

An ETW event by itself would not establish that anything leaves the machine. ETW is used for plenty of local diagnostics. The more revealing question was who was listening to this particular report.

The VM already had a Diagtrack-Listener session subscribed to both ends of the path. These PowerShell queries showed its subscriptions:

The first subscription, for KernelProcess , had MatchAnyKeyword=0x400000000002 , which includes the summary's 0x400000000000 keyword. The second, for Microsoft.Windows.MissionControlAggregator , had MatchAnyKeyword=0xe00000000000 , which includes the report's 0x800000000000 keyword. Both had level 255 .

The subscription showed where the report could go. To check whether Windows actually queued it for transmission, I inspected DiagTrack's EventStore.db and decompressed the JSON batches in its AsimovEvents table. This revealed an important condition: the agent-usage report is treated as optional diagnostic data .

When optional diagnostic data is allowed (enabled by default in the US setup I tested), Windows queues the coding-agent usage report for upload to Microsoft. I verified this by finding the agent event itself in DiagTrack's upload queue:

I checked this with a clean installation of Windows 11 Home ARM64 using the latest official ISO, with the region set to the United States. Before changing any privacy settings, the Diagnostic data toggle was already enabled and labeled Include Optional . After completing setup with those defaults, AllowTelemetry was 3 , confirming that optional diagnostic data was enabled.

Optional diagnostic data is therefore enabled by default, at least in the US setup I tested. If you did not opt out of it during installation or disable optional diagnostic data later, it is still enabled and your coding agent usage data is being uploaded. You can decline optional diagnostics during setup or turn off Send optional diagnostic data later under Settings → Privacy & security → Diagnostics & feedback . Microsoft's diagnostics and privacy guide explains how to change it.

items.title: Atp Finals: Cobolli stecca la prima, con Medvedev una sconfitta che brucia: il russo vince in due set
items.summary: Ora ci vuole un'impresa per le semifinali
items.content:
Ce l'ha messa tutta, ha usato ogni energia e adottato ogni strategia ma non è bastato: Flavio Cobolli inciampa all'esordio delle Atp Finals di Torino ed esce battuto dalla sfida con il russo Daniil Medvedev. Una sconfitta che, per come è maturata, brucia. Niente di pregiudicato per l'accesso alle semifinali ma il percorso ora è tutto in salita: dovrà superare Frances Tiafoe e 'sua maestà' Carlos Alcaraz, apparso oggi in gran forma, per passare al secondo turno.

Tensione dipinta sul volto di Cobolli già all'ingresso in campo, in un'Inalpi Arena tutto esaurito. Il match con Medvedev è partito subito "a mille": servizio spesso decisivo e scambi veloci da fondo campo. Una partita giocata a viso aperto da due giocatori molto simili, incollati a fondo campo. Il russo è parso solido al servizio, per Flavio invece già il secondo turno di battuta è stato complicato: sotto 15-40 è riuscito a recuperare anche grazie al caloroso sostegno del pubblico. Stessa storia al nono game. A fare il tifo per il romano alcuni compagni ed ex compagni in nazionale, Berrettini addirittura nel box, Sonego e Fognini sugli spalti. La partita è così filata via fino al tiebreak, dove Medvedev si è dimostrato più freddo nei momenti salienti e ha portato a casa il set.

La musica non è cambiata nel secondo parziale. I due hanno continuato a giocare "a specchio", picchiando le palline senza risparmiarsi. La svolta al settimo game. Cobolli ha avuto un passaggio a vuoto e sul 30-40 ha tirato in corridoio un comodo diritto, concedendo il break. A questo punto recuperare il match con un cagnaccio come Medvedev è diventata una vera impresa. Le energie fisiche e mentali sono venute a mancare al romano, la partita ormai era indirizzata. Il russo, esperienza da vendere, non ha vacillato e ha chiuso 6-3.

"C'era una grande atmosfera - ha detto Medvedev a fine partita - il pubblico chiaramente ha tifato per Flavio ma ho sentito che mi sosteneva quando facevo delle belle cose. E' stata una bellissima sfida, sono molto contento di questa vittoria. Nel 2026 ho giocato un tennis migliore rispetto all'anno precedente, ho servito meglio. Stasera ho servito molto bene e questo mi ha aiutato a vincere la partita".

Flavio Cobolli tornerà in campo mercoledì prossimo - orario da definire - contro lo statunitense Tiafoe. A completare la 'giornata nera' per gli azzurri alle Atp Finals anche la sconfitta del doppio Simone Bolelli-Andrea Vavassori: sono stati superati in due set dall'argentino Horacio Zeballos e dallo spagnolo Marcel Granollers con un duplice 6-4.

"L'assenza di Jannik alle Atp Finals non mi aiuta perché comunque mi avrebbe tolto un po' di pressione. A noi italiani inconsciamente ci dà una grande mano fuori dal campo, se la prende un po' tutta lui la pressione e il dover vincere, i fan. A noi ci lascia un po' di spazio, ci lascia anche un po' di margine di errore, le nostre sconfitte pesano di meno e questo durante l'anno si fa sentire". Lo ha detto Flavio Cobolli nella conferenza stampa al termine del match perso contro Daniil Medvedev alle Atp Finals di Torino. "Oggi credo di aver fatto una prestazione sopra la media di quello che mi aspettavo prima della partita - ha aggiunto - però poi c'è anche l'avversario e oggi l'avversario è stato più forte di me. Oggi la tensione non ha influito sul gioco, è stato più merito del mio avversario che demerito mio". Infine sulla presenza di Berrettini nel suo box: "Noi siamo sempre in contatto, non siamo solamente colleghi, ma credo che siamo in primis grandi amici, parliamo un po' di tutto, non solo di tennis, il nostro rapporto va oltre a questo lavoro. Ho saputo alle 19,30 che sarebbe venuto, mi ha mandato un messaggio all'ultimo minuto. Gli ho chiesto espressamente se gli avrebbe fatto piacere fare parte del team e mi ha risposto di sì. Quindi ho parlato con il mio team e gli ho detto che avevo la necessità di avere Matteo in mezzo a loro, che mi avrebbe dato una grande mano".

"Ho servito bene e questo mi ha dato molta fiducia. Sentivo che se servivo nel punto giusto al momento giusto, non avrei subito il break. Ho messo molta pressione addosso a Cobolli e ne ho tolta parecchia a me stesso. Pensavo solo: 'Ok, devo fare qualcosina in risposta, mettere dentro qualche risposta, lottare un po' e metterò ancora più pressione'. E prima o poi questa pressione avrebbe dovuto dare i suoi frutti, ed è proprio quello che è successo". Così Daniil Medvedev, nella conferenza stampa dopo il match vinto contro Flavio Cobolli alle Atp Finals di Torino, ha raccontato come ha interpretato la sfida. Tra i prossimi avversari c'è anche Carlos Alcaraz: "E' un giocatore straordinario - sottolinea il russo - e può battere chiunque e ovunque. Ha giocato la finale qui l'anno scorso e ha perso solo contro Jannik. Penso però che questo campo sia la migliore opportunità per batterlo. Potrei ottenere qualche punto facile al servizio e magari mettere a segno qualche vincente perché è veloce, cosa non facile da fare contro di lui perché è probabilmente il giocatore più mobile che abbiamo mai visto".

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
items.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.content:
Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort.

Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's ​access to AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since his departure, supporters have launched an online petition demanding his return.

Musk and Sweeny are among the more than 175,000 who have signed the open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by a make up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive.

They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".

President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.

"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models.

The move came ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jingping this week.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted to China.

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times , external , though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".

Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China.

"They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that," he said.

Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.

Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.

The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.

Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X. , external

"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."

But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".

Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.

Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.

For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

items.title: How to Break into Security, Ptacek Edition (2012)
items.summary: Article URL: https://krebsonsecurity.com/2012/06/how-to-break-into-security-ptacek-edition/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50524225 Points: 67 # Comments: 16
items.content:
At least once a month, sometimes more, readers write in to ask how they can break into the field of computer security. Some of the emails are from people in jobs that have nothing to do with security, but who are fascinated enough by the field to contemplate a career change. Others are already in an information technology position but are itching to segue into security. I always respond with my own set of stock answers, but each time I do this, I can’t help but feel my advice is incomplete, or at least not terribly well-rounded.

I decided to ask some of the brightest minds in the security industry today what advice they’d give. Almost everyone I asked said they, too, frequently get asked the very same question, but each had surprisingly different takes on the subject. Today is the first installment in a series of responses to this question. When the last of the advice columns have run, I’ll create an archive of them all that will be anchored somewhere prominently on the home page. That way, the next time someone asks how they can break into security, I’ll have more to offer than just my admittedly narrow perspectives on the matter.

Last month, I interviewed Thomas Ptacek , founder of Matasano Security , about how companies could beef up password security in the wake of a week full of news about password leaks at LinkedIn and other online businesses. Ptacek’s provocative advice generated such a huge amount of reader interest and further discussion that I thought it made sense to begin this series with his thoughts:

Ptacek: “Information security is one of the most interesting, challenging, and, if you do it carefully, rewarding fields in the technology industry. It’s one of the few technology jobs where the most fun roles are well compensated. If you grew up dreaming of developing games, the laws of supply and demand teach a harsh lesson early in your career: game development jobs are often tedious and usually pay badly. But if you watched “Sneakers” and ideated a life spent breaking or defending software, great news: infosec can be more fun in real life, and it’s fairly lucrative.

I’m a software developer. I try to look at security through the lens of computer science. To me, the most attractive thing about the field is the opportunity it provides to work with lots of different concepts at lots of different levels. Computer security might be the best way to work professionally with compiler theory, or to spend time understanding computer microarchitecture, or to apply advanced mathematics.

Other people get involved in security for different reasons, and those reasons are probably equally valid. Some people really like the “good guys / bad guys” narrative that comes with security. Some people see security as an opportunity to save the world. Other people are drawn to the competitive nature of the field: at the higher levels, it really is a cat-and-mouse game. It also comes closer to meritocracy than most of technology: you can either break in or you can’t; your defenses either work or they don’t.

But for me, it’s just one of the best development jobs you can get, and with that in mind, here’s my advice for people interested in pursuing a career in it.

First: I want you to learn how to program. Clearly, you can get through college and get a good-paying steady job without ever learning to love programming. But no one factor gives you as much control over your career, as much of an ability to write your own ticket, as the ability to solve problems using programming languages. A lot of very smart technology professionals have concluded that they just don’t enjoy writing software. Those people should reconsider. Try different languages, or different application domains, but find a way to make programming stick in your head.

Second: the best jobs in our field are in application security. You can get good steady work designing firewall deployments, setting up desktop agents, or responding to incidents. But all those roles are fundamentally reacting to what’s happening in appsec. The next generation of security products — along with the org charts of security teams at the savviest companies — are being designed now, by accident, by application security practitioners.

Appsec roles are roles that involve attacking software or devising fixes and countermeasures for those attacks. Two good ways to “come up” in appsec: become a penetration tester, or contribute to (or start) a secure software development practice in your company.

A good way to move into penetration testing: grab some industry standard tools and use an Amazon EC2 account to set up a “shooting range” to attack. Some of the best-known tools are available for free: the Nessus scanner , for instance, while not an application security tool, is free and can land you a network penetration testing role that you can use as a springboard to breaking applications.

When people reach out to Matasano asking how to get a foot in the door attacking software, we have a few simple steps to offer:

0. Learn to love programming in at least one language. The C Programming Language has the most cachet in application security, but for this step-by-step list, Java or Python or Ruby will do fine.

2. Go to the “previous releases” archive at WordPress.org and grab very old versions of WordPress; install them at EC2.

3. Download OWASP WebScarab or Burp Suite Free Edition , both of which are free, and use them to find bugs in ancient WordPress.

If you’re already in an IT role, and want to come up on the defensive side of appsec, try to position yourself near custom software development. Most large firms build “line of business” applications. As a rule, building “line of business” isn’t particularly fun. But defending those apps can be; sometimes, the most boring applications turn out to be surprisingly sensitive.

And the good news for doing appsec in BigCo’s: most companies have very immature security programs. If you can get a role in QA, or in what the cool kids are calling “DevOps”, you can end up with a lot of influence in security. At Matasano, we’ve watched lots of ops people successfully transition to appsec and senior security management just by instituting basic security testing processes on their company’s software.

To me, the whole field boils down to studying, understanding, and manipulating technology. Like most software security practices, we’ve gotten our hands dirty with a fascinating cross-section of the whole technology industry. We’ve written attack tools that target the control registers of device chipsets, we’ve done custom RF work, we’ve written low-level debuggers for different CPU architectures, and we’ve seen and beaten up on products built in almost every programming language and every platform you can imagine. If crawling through the ventilation ducts of the world’s most important technology is something you think might make you tick like we do… well, appsec! Learn to code. Spend a couple days Starbucks money on an EC2 account and deploy some broken apps to break. Find opportunities to practice in your job.

And, uh, come talk to us? People like you are hard to find!”

items.title: Sanchez e Lula 'uniti in difesa delle istituzioni contro la minaccia ultradestra'
items.summary: Incontro alla Moncloa a due settimane dalle elezioni in Spagna
items.content:
Il premier spagnolo Pedro Sanchez e il presidente brasiliano Luiz Ignacio Lula da Silva hanno avuto oggi a Madrid un colloquio sul futuro delle Nazioni Unite e l'ordine internazionale e "sull'importanza di difendere le istituzioni democratiche e la coesione sociale a fronte dell'avanzata dell'estrema destra". Lo segnalano fonti della Moncloa. I due leader hanno anche discusso sull'agenda bilaterale "per continuare a rafforzare i legami economici e sociali fra Spagna e Brasile", aggiungono.

Al di là dell'incontro istituzionale, i due leader hanno esibito piena sintonia politica nella campagna per le elezioni politiche in Spagna del 29 novembre. Lula, alla sua prima visita nel Paese, dopo la vittoria alle ultime presidenziali in Brasile, è un punto di riferimento per Sanchez nella battaglia contro "l'internazionale di ultradestra" in cui vede allineati il presidente Usa Donald Trump, quello argentino Javier Milei o i Bolsonaro in Brasile, assieme al leader del Partito Popolare, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, e a quello della forza di estrema destra Vox, Santiago Abascal.

Il capo dell'esecutivo spagnolo, in svantaggio nei sondaggi, punta a emulare l'esempio di Lula nella "remontada", la rimonta compiuta dal presidente brasiliano al secondo turno delle presidenziali, quando è riuscito a invertire il distacco sull'avversario Flavio Bolsonaro.

Il leader brasiliano del Partito dei Lavoratori avrebbe dovuto intervenire oggi a un confronto pubblico con il segretario e candidato alla rielezione del Psoe presso la sede madrilena del sindacato Ugt, cancellato a causa di un'afonia di Lula, che gli ha impedito anche di intervenire nel fine settimana al vertice del clima Cop31 ad Antalya, in Turchia.

items.title: Cobolli cede con Medvedev e si rabbuia, Tiafoe perde con Alcaraz sorridendo
items.summary: La rubrica Monday’s Net sulle Atp Finals
items.content:
Alle 20.49 Flavio Cobolli entra nel catino blu dell'Inalpi Arena accolto dal boato che compete a un gladiatore (però a me lui ricorda Caio Gregorio, "er guardiano der Pretorio", citazione per boomers only). Con il suo avversario, Daniil Medvedev, il pubblico è più tiepido. Stasera Flavio può contare sugli sguardi e i consigli del fratellone Matteo, che di cognome fa Berrettini, nel 2019 primo italiano tra i Grandi Maestri dell'era ATP, a Londra. L'atmosfera è sovreccitata come nella serata inaugurale delle esordienti ATP Finals torinesi, il 14 novembre 2021. Allora Berrettini giocava contro Alexander Zverev : perse il primo set al tie-break e si fermò all'inizio del secondo per una lesione agli addominali obliqui. Si ritirò in lacrime. Fu Jannik Sinner a sostituirlo.

Il match è equilibrato. Però il russo serve appena un po' meglio e riesce più spesso a uscire vittorioso dagli scambi prolungati, come accade anche nel tie-break del primo set. Gli basta. Nel secondo parziale il break decisivo glielo regala Flavio nel settimo game con un paio di colpi fuori misura per eccesso di fretta e ansia. C'è poco altro da raccontare. Una sconfitta per 7-6 6-3 contro uno dei più titolati giocatori del circuito è tutto fuorché disonorevole. E comunque serve per rompere il ghiaccio.

Nel pomeriggio Carlos Alcaraz impiega 69 minuti per mostrare quanta distanza corra oggi tra lui e gli avversari: quelli in attività, non gli assenti, ovviamente. Carlitos arriva a Torino con i titoli di Vienna e Parigi in valigia e gioca subito come fa chi non ha tempo da perdere. Risponde a Frances Tiafoe con i piedi dentro il campo, toglie il respiro allo scambio già dal secondo colpo, alterna con naturalezza le accelerazioni di dritto e rovescio alla palla corta. Nei suoi turni di servizio non concede quasi appigli. Nel secondo set il break arriva al terzo gioco e da quel momento la partita smette di essere una contesa per diventare una dimostrazione. Il 6-2 6-2 si racconta con pochi altri numeri: quattro giochi di fila in avvio, primo set archiviato in 27 minuti, quattro break complessivi, tre palle break annullate nell'unico momento in cui l'americano prova a rimettere in discussione qualcosa.

Nella sessione diurna c'è da registrare la sconfitta di Simone Bolelli e Andrea Vavassori , che cedono un turno di battuta in entrambi i set ai fortissimi Marcel Granollers e Horacio Zeballos , quest'anno affrontati in due occasioni importanti: li hanno sconfitti in finale agli Internazionali, le hanno buscate in semifinale al Roland Garros. Oggi hanno perso di nuovo per 6-4 6-4. Il consuntivo adesso è di quattro vittorie a testa. Poi fa buio e cambia il pubblico. All'apertura della sessione serale, davanti agli ingressi dell'arena, la folla preme, code lunghe, biglietti in mano, qualche bandiera tricolore. Tra un paio d'ore tocca a Flavio, che ha qualcosa che ai torinesi sembra piacere assai: è un eroe raggiungibile, che si può toccare senza il rischio che ti stacchino il braccio. Non un fenomeno che viene tenuto sotto una cappa (seppure di vetro), ma un ragazzo che è arrivato tra i primi otto del mondo un passo alla volta, sbagliando e ripartendo. Il pomeriggio ha mostrato cos'è l'eccezione. La sera promette la possibilità di tifare per qualcuno che ci somiglia. Poi va come va.Ma prima di dare il via agli scambi con Medvedev è prevista la cerimonia di premiazione del giocatore che chiude da numero 1 la stagione: che è Zverev, mica Sinner, dominatore del ranking da aprile fino a due settimane fa. Emozionatissimo, Alexander ringrazia e chiama accanto a sé il padre, poi la mamma, la nonna, il fratello, la nipotina, perfino due dei cagnetti di famiglia. Manca la figlia Mayla, che ha cinque anni e spesso spunta con lui in giro per il mondo: ma forse questa settimana dev'essere l'ex compagna Brenda Patea a tenerla con sé. Così oggi Sascha rappresenta anche i padri single, che non sono pochi.

items.title: Il Papa lascia il suo Perù, ultima tappa di una visita storica
items.summary: In 11 giorni seguito da 15 milioni di fedeli, un successo sulle tracce di Francesco
items.content:
"Grazie Perù, mi sono sentito a casa. Che Dio ti benedica". Sono le parole di Leone XIV, commosso ma felice, al termine della Messa nella spianata di Las Palmas, nella capitale del suo Perù, ultima funzione del giorno finale di una visita che in Sudamerica tutti definiscono storica, per il suo impatto religioso, sociale, ma anche politico .

Il Pontefice è stato accolto ovunque da una marea di gente entusiasta: si stima che abbia incontrato circa 15 milioni di persone in 11 giorni, toccando dieci città di tre Paesi, Uruguay, Argentina e il suo Perù. Una missione, sin dal primo momento, sulle orme del suo predecessore, Papa Bergoglio, primo papa sudamericano della storia. Anche la funzione di oggi, quella del commiato, davanti a un milione e mezzo di persone, si è svolta nella spianata de Las Palmas, dove Francesco tenne una messa uguale, ma nel gennaio del 2018. Malgrado le alte temperature, spesso oltre i 30 gradi, e le grandi alture - ieri ha celebrato messa sulle Ande, a oltre 3000 metri - Prevost ha superato ogni difficoltà in perfetta forma fisica.

Un dato non scontato se si pensa che poco più di un mese fa venne sottoposto a una operazione al polmone, con l'asportazione di un tumore. Una missione dal profondo significato sociale: il Papa di fronte a presidenti sovranisti, come l'argentino Javier Milei e la peruviana Keiko Fujimori, ha parlato agli ultimi, ai giovani senza lavoro, alle famiglie povere, agli anziani soli, esortando i governi a seguire la Dottrina sociale della Chiesa. A Chilayo, la sua ex diocesi, dove si sentiva a casa, ha chiesto il rispetto dei diritti umani, dell'ambiente, la tutela degli immigrati, dei nativi amazzonici. Quindi ha affrontato senza timidezze il capitolo degli abusi da parte di esponenti del clero chiedendo alla Chiesa "un impegno più deciso" per contrastare questo triste fenomeno. Bisogna rispondere "come farebbe Gesù, con verità, giustizia, perdono e riparazione", ha detto. Infine, dopo aver ricordato che la famiglia naturale è formata solo da una donna e un uomo, da cui scaturisce "la maternità e la paternità, la figliolanza e la fraternità", si è scagliato contro "il persistere della mentalità machista", che si manifesta "negli abusi e nelle violenze contro le donne". E ha lanciato "un appello urgente: valorizziamo le donne! Proteggiamo e rispettiamo le bambine!".

items.title: Spamhaus new email sender requirements in November
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.spamhaus.org/sender-guidelines/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50523784 Points: 67 # Comments: 51
items.content:
Starting in November 2026 , we are gradually rolling out a requirement for every sending IP to have a valid HELO, a reverse DNS (PTR) record, and a matching A record. Use the HELO checker below to see whether the DNS meets our best practices, and follow the guidelines to avoid being listed.

Guidance for senders, mail admins, and postmasters on meeting Spamhaus's sending requirements. All senders must meet these minimum email sending requirements to avoid being listed.

Each recipient should confirm their address by clicking a link in a confirmation email. If no confirmation is received, do not send email to that address. Purchased, rented and harvested lists are the most common source of spam trap hits, and hitting traps is one of the fastest routes to a listing. See section

Every sending IP must have a reverse DNS entry pointing to a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). That hostname must, in turn, resolve back to the same sending IP address. This is known as forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS). An IP with missing or mismatched reverse DNS is treated as suspicious and is one of the most common reasons for an IP to be considered for listing. See section

The hostname the server announces in the HELO/EHLO command must resolve to the IP it is connecting from, and must stay consistent across connections from that IP. Placeholder values, hosting-provider defaults, and hostnames that vary between connections are treated as signals of misconfiguration or compromise and can result in a listing. See section

If sending over IPv6, the sending address must fall within an allocation of /64 or larger (a /64 is the standard block size we recommend assigning), and that space must have valid reverse DNS. IPv6 ranges without reverse DNS or with allocations smaller than /64 are often misused by spammers. See section

Publish SPF and DMARC records for every sending domain, sign every outbound message with a signature, and align the DKIM sending domain with the domain in the message's RFC 5322 From address. Authentication is one of the signals that shapes reputation, so gaps here make a listing more likely when other signals are weak. See section

All sending infrastructure must have the following DNS and mailserver configuration. Failure to do so can result in IPs being listed on the Email Spam IPs (CSS) or compromised IPs (XBL) zones.

Ensure the sending IP address has a valid reverse DNS (rDNS) entry resolving to a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the sending IP address. Spamhaus will treat emails originating from IP addresses without rDNS as suspicious and this will be reflected in the IP's reputation, and receivers using Spamhaus data may subject it to additional filtering.

Ensure the rDNS hostname resolves to the connecting IP address via a corresponding forward DNS (A/AAAA) record .

Abusive actors often rely on the reputation of upstream DNS records to hide their identity. Instead, configure a branded reverse DNS to use the sender's own domain, to improve trust signals for the IP address.

items.title: The Donald sostiene Mr. Nvidia, 'una buona idea il suo rientro'
items.summary: E difende Lutnick. Titolo giù alla vigilia della trimestrale. Altman: 'Huang un mio eroe'
items.content:
La campagna a sostegno di Jensen Huang arruola il nome più illustre: Donald Trump. "Non è una cattiva idea, non mi dispiacerebbe affatto vederlo tornare", ha commentato il presidente Usa, a proposito del reintegro di Mr. Nvidia alla guida del colosso dei microchip per l'IA. Un'ipotesi riportata dal Financial Times ("sta valutando un ritorno" e "ne ha discusso con persone di fiducia") che si basa anche sul crescente slancio delle oltre 175mila firme raccolte dalla petizione 'Stand With Jensen' ('Stiamo con Jensen'), lanciata dai guru della Silicon Valley e spostata in pieno da Elon Musk.

Una mobilitazione a cui Sam Altman, il patron di OpenAI, tra le startup Usa di punta dell'intelligenza artificiale, ha dato una sua spiegazione: "E' da tempo un mio eroe, gli eroi hanno difetti. Sono grato per l'azienda che ha costruito. Provo una forte empatia personale per una situazione come questa. Ricordo com'era, anche se sembra un'eternità fa", ha detto Altman a un evento di Semafor. "Ma è difficile immaginare la rivoluzione dell'IA senza Jensen. E l'azienda che ha costruito ha scommesso su di noi fin dall'inizio. Noi abbiamo scommesso su di lui fin dall'inizio. Gli sono immensamente grato per questo", ha concluso.

Tuttavia, a dispetto delle pressioni, il board della compagnia "non sta valutando" il ritorno di Huang alla carica, in base a fonti sentite dalla Cnbc, alla vigilia della presentazione della trimestrale di Nvidia (altro tonfo al Nasdaq, -4%) che sarà l'esordio di Colette Kress, la direttrice finanziaria nominata ceo ad interim, al posto di Huang, travolto dallo scandalo delle relazioni extraconiugali, di cui una con Alice Huang, ex top executive di Megaspeed, società basata a Singapore che avrebbe stornato illegalmente verso il Dragone i microchip più innovativi.

Trump, che per il Washington Post possedeva a fine agosto azioni Nvidia del valore fino a 62 milioni di dollari, ha detto di non ritenere che la vicenda abbia mai messo a rischio la sicurezza nazionale, di non "essere sicuro che Alice Huang sia una spia" e di non essere mai stato informato dal segretario di Stato e consigliere per la Sicurezza nazionale Marco Rubio sul caso Nvidia ("mai sentito"). Tuttavia, la vicenda ha creato forti turbolenze nell'amministrazione americana: il segretario al Tesoro Scott Bessent, che ha chiesto che Nvidia si doti di un ceo esterno, ha attaccato il segretario al Commercio Howard Lutnick, addebitando al suo dipartimento gli ostacoli contro i tentativi di altri dicasteri di alzare i controlli anti-Cina sull'export dei microchip e di una stretta su Megaspeed. Il tycoon ha detto di non avere alcuna intenzione di licenziare Lutnick ("ha svolto un ottimo lavoro"), ma nel frattempo di Dipartimento del Commercio ha emanato una norma provvisoria per limitare l'accesso remoto a chip e server per l'Ia avanzata da parte di alcuni Paesi per stroncare il fenomeno della 'riesportazione'.

Intanto, il Congresso vuole capire se Nvidia abbia svolto attività di lobbying per influenzare il dibattito sull'export di chip verso la Repubblica popolare cinese, mentre lo scandalo "minaccia l'offensiva di corteggiamento della Cina in vista del vertice con Trump", ha rilevato il Wall Street Journal, mentre il tycoon era in volo per l'Asia. A Shenzhen, a margine dell'Apec, incontrerà Xi Jinping. Infine, Anthropic: farà il suo esordio giovedì al Nasdaq e la posta in gioco è altissima per quasi tutte le principali aziende tecnologiche. Amd, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia e Tmsc stanno investendo 26 miliardi totali al prezzo di Ipo, stimato tra i 70 e i 78 dollari per azione, per una valutazione della compagnia di circa 1.500 miliardi.

Nvidia chiude in calo a Wall Street, dove i titoli perdono il 4,12% alla vigilia della trimestrale.

items.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
items.summary: The Iran-backed Houthis are gaining ground and their advance could have dangerous consequences, writes the BBC's security correspondent.
items.content:
The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden.

Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world.

Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula.

The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears.

Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.

In normal times, it accounts for around 12% of global trade, with anywhere between 70 to 150 ships a day making the transit.

But not any more. Although the Houthis say they are no threat to maritime traffic, they are currently at war with Saudi Arabia, making it extremely hazardous for the Saudis to send their oil tankers past the now rebel-controlled coast.

When the US and Israel started a war with Iran in February, Tehran responded by choking off much of the oil trade flowing out of the Gulf through another narrow chokepoint - the Strait of Hormuz. This sent oil prices soaring, boosted inflation and hurt economies everywhere.

The Saudis had a Plan B. Instead of exporting their oil past the dangerous coast of Iran, where their tankers risked being droned or mined by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, they started pumping it overland through their East-West Pipeline to an export terminal on the Red Sea at Yanbu. This worked for a while.

But then in July a cold truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis broke down, that pipeline got hit by drones and the rebels started firing missiles and drones at targets all over Saudi Arabia.

On land, the Houthis seized the initiative and made a lightning dash down the Red Sea coast, sending the Yemeni army into headlong retreat. A brief counter-offensive appears to have failed and the Houthis are now reported to be in full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the nearby offshore islands.

Nicholas Hopton, a former British Ambassador to both Yemen and Iran and now director-general of the UK-based Middle East Association, says: "The decision by the legitimate government of Yemen to prioritise the military defence of Aden at the expense of withdrawing from other areas suggests that the war is not going well for the Saudi-backed [Yemeni] government. And the rest of the world should be worried."

He warns that if the port of Aden – a city of roughly 1.25 million inhabitants – was to fall to the Houthis, it "would undoubtedly precipitate a further escalation in the regional crisis and further fragility in the global economy, catalysed by the US-Iran war".

But Mohammed al-Basha, the Yemeni founder of the US-based risk advisory firm Basha Report, believes the Houthis would struggle to capture the heavily fortified city of Aden.

"Any attempt to seize a densely populated city like Aden would come at a significant human cost," Basha said. "Advancing across the flat coastal plains would also expose Houthi forces to air power."

"For now, the Houthis appear to be seeking a negotiated surrender, hoping to exploit infighting and divisions among southern factions to achieve their objectives without a costly urban offensive."

It is conceivable that the Yemen war will settle into a less dramatic but deeply unsatisfactory stasis - a situation where casualty figures subside yet the country remains split between areas controlled by the Houthis - Iran's Shia allies - and the disparate and often poorly motivated forces of the Saudi-backed Yemeni army.

The former British defence attaché to Yemen, Col Iain Smailes, warned that the recent Houthi advance could trigger a spike in oil prices, as it did when they seized the Bab al-Mandab Strait in September.

He also warns this could have a knock-on effect to security well beyond Yemen's borders.

"By extending their control over the western coastline, the Houthis will increase their ability to smuggle weapons and ammunition from Iran, the Horn of Africa and elsewhere, posing additional threats to the region," Col Smailes said.

"This control will enable both Iran and the Houthis to extend their influence in East Africa and beyond."
